title.narrative: Enhancing value chains and markets of Neglected and Underutilized crop Species to contribute to Agroecological transition in Africa
Migliorare le catene del valore e i mercati delle specie neglette e sottoutilizzate per contribuire alla transizione agroecologica in Africa

description.narrative: AgrEcoNUS+ aims to enhance food and nutrition security, climate resilience, and socio-economic inclusion in Sub-Saharan Africa by strengthening sustainable value chains rooted in neglected and underutilized crop species (NUS) through agroecological approaches. The project, pursuing and expanding upon lessons learned and achievements realized in previous initiatives, promotes the transition toward resilient food systems, combining local knowledge, innovation, and multi-stakeholder governance for market development and increasing demand for NUS-based and agroecological products. The logic of the initiative is based on the strengthened integration of NUS and agroecology in local agri-food systems, acting on three interconnected results: sustainable and resilient agricultural production through the promotion of NUS and agroecological practices, achieved through the documentation of traditional knowledge, scientific research, and capacity building. The promotion of a political-institutional environment favorable to agrobiodiversity, local seed systems, and agroecological systems. The support for markets and consumption by promoting NUS/agroecological value chains to increase consumer access to and trust in diverse and nutritious foods. Implemented in nine countries in Western, Eastern, and Southern Africa, the project targets three main groups (value chain actors, decision-makers/institutions, and academic institutions), promoting female and youth inclusivity, and involving a partnership of over forty African and European partners. The initiative aligns its objectives with continental and global frameworks (e.g., African Union's Agendas, EU Green Deal), positioning NUS as a driver of sustainable and inclusive development.

AgrEcoNUS+ mira a potenziare la sicurezza alimentare e nutrizionale, la resilienza climatica e l'inclusione socio-economica in Africa Subsahariana, rafforzando le catene del valore sostenibili basate sulle specie neglette e sottoutilizzate (NUS) tramite l'agroecologia. Il progetto, perseguendo ed espandendo quanto appreso e realizzato in iniziative precedenti come Sustlives e Orph-Crops, promuove la transizione verso sistemi alimentari resilienti, combinando conoscenza locale, innovazione e governance multi-stakeholder per lo sviluppo dei mercati e l'aumento della domanda per prodotti basati sulle NUS e rispettosi dei principi agroecologici. La logica dell’iniziativa si fonda sull'integrazione rafforzata di NUS e agroecologia nei sistemi agroalimentari locali, agendo su tre risultati interconnessi: la produzione agricola sostenibile e resiliente attraverso la promozione delle NUS e pratiche agroecologiche, attraverso la documentazione del sapere tradizionale, la ricerca scientifica e l'accrescimento delle capacità. La promozione di un contesto politico-istituzionale favorevole all’agrobiodiversità, ai sistemi sementieri locali e ai sistemi agroecologici. Il sostegno ai mercati e ai consumi promuovendo catene del valore NUS/agroecologiche per aumentare l'accesso e la fiducia dei consumatori in alimenti diversi e nutrienti. Implementato in nove paesi in Africa Occidentale, Orientale e Meridionale, il progetto mira a tre gruppi target principali (attori della catena del valore, decisori/istituzioni e istituzioni accademiche), promuovendo l’inclusività femminile e giovanile e coinvolgendo una partnership di oltre quaranta partner africani ed europei. L’iniziativa allinea gli obiettivi con i framework continentali e globali (es. African Union's Agendas, EU Green Deal), posizionando le NUS come motore di sviluppo sostenibile e inclusivo.

tag.narrative: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls

By 2020, maintain the genetic diversity of seeds, cultivated plants and farmed and domesticated animals and their related wild species, including through soundly managed and diversified seed and plant banks at the national, regional and international levels, and promote access to and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as internationally agreed
By 2030, achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources

By 2030, build the resilience of the poor and those in vulnerable situations and reduce their exposure and vulnerability to climate-related extreme events and other economic, social and environmental shocks and disasters

By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment
By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round

By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality

By 2030, ensure that all men and women, in particular the poor and the vulnerable, have equal rights to economic resources, as well as access to basic services, ownership and control over land and other forms of property, inheritance, natural resources, appropriate new technology and financial services, including microfinance
End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture
End poverty in all its forms everywhere
Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters in all countries
Support developing countries to strengthen their scientific and technological capacity to move towards more sustainable patterns of consumption and production
Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts

Undertake reforms to give women equal rights to economic resources, as well as access to ownership and control over land and other forms of property, financial services, inheritance and natural resources, in accordance with national laws
